import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 324

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/324](https://www.erdosproblems.com/324)
-/

open scoped Polynomial

namespace Erdos324

/--
Does there exist a polynomial $f(x)\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ such that all the sums $f(a)+f(b)$ with
$a < b$ nonnegative integers are distinct?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_324 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ f : ℤ[X], {(a, b) : ℕ × ℕ | a < b}.InjOn fun (a, b) => f.eval (a : ℤ) + f.eval (b : ℤ) := by
  sorry

/--
Probably $f(x) = x^5$ has the property that the sums $f(a)+f(b)$ with
$a < b$ nonnegative integers are distinct.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_324.variants.quintic : {(a, b) : ℕ × ℕ | a < b}.InjOn fun (a, b) => a ^ 5 + b ^ 5 := by
  sorry

end Erdos324

reformulations.difference: The source proposes the integer polynomial f(x)=x^5; Lean directly asserts injectivity of the natural-number sum a^5+b^5 on pairs with a<b.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Evaluating (Polynomial.X^5 : ℤ[X]) at a natural number cast to ℤ gives its fifth power in ℤ. The embedding ℕ → ℤ preserves addition and powers and reflects equality. Consequently, equality of the natural-number sums is equivalent to equality of the polynomial-evaluation sums, so the two restricted-injectivity statements are equivalent.

review.notes: Both declarations faithfully match the source's explicit nonnegative-input and strict a<b conditions. The main answer slot has the correct propositional type and global scope. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, I proved the expansion of InjOn into coordinatewise uniqueness, ruled out all constant polynomial witnesses, checked evaluations at 0, 1 and 2, and tested all 5,050 pairs with 0≤a<b≤100 without finding a fifth-power collision. Direct access to erdosproblems.com was blocked by Cloudflare; the full archived source and current companion status data were used instead. Neither records a status discrepancy.
